column3: Text

Certain duties require the transporting of items to a designated location.

While carrying out such tasks, use of actions will be restricted, and you will be granted the **Transporting** status effect.

You must be wary of attacks, as they will sap your strength.
You will lose the Transporting status when the effect duration expires or you change areas. In such cases, you may return to the starting location and begin anew.

During certain duties, you may gain the **Transparent** status effect, which restricts available actions but allows you to pass by most enemies undetected. Use this invisible state to reach your destination before the effect expires.

You will lose the Transparent status when the effect duration expires or you change areas, causing nearby enemies to detect you and preventing quest progression.

You may return to the starting location at any time to refresh the duration of the Transparent status. If it has already expired, it will be granted anew.

Certain duties require that one or more NPCs accompany you in order to proceed with quest objectives.

You must keep them at your side and make your way to a designated location.

So long as you remain in the same area, NPCs accompanying you will remain at your side even when using Teleport or the Aethernet.

It is possible to ride mounts or swim while escorting NPCs. Please note, however, they will not appear at your side until you dismount or leave the water.

You may also speak with NPCs while escorting them. Furthermore, you may encounter “conversation points” along the way which offer additional topics of discussion. These points will also be indicated on your map.

When speaking with NPCs, you will be given the option to part ways. You will also part ways automatically when changing areas.

If you part ways with an NPC, you may return to the starting point and speak with them to try again.
Certain duties require you to follow an NPC to a designated location. Should you fall too far behind, the NPC will return to the starting point, and you must speak with them to try again.
Certain duties require you to follow an NPC and approach without being seen. Should you be detected, you must return to the starting point and try again.
The indicator shown in the image above indicates that you risk being seen should the NPC you're following turn around.
The indicator shown in the image above indicates that you risk being seen should you be standing too close to the NPC.

Certain duties require you to transform into creatures or other people, restricting available actions. These transformations only last a limited time, indicated by the **Transfiguration** status effect.

Should the Transfiguration status effect expire, or you stray too far from the objective, you will be returned to your original form.

You may return to the starting location at any time to refresh the duration of the Transfiguration status. If it has already expired, it will be granted anew.
Certain duties require you to don a disguise to complete quest objectives. You may only remain disguised for a limited time, indicated by the **Guise** status effect.

Should the Guise status effect expire, or you stray too far from the objective, you will lose your disguise.

You may return to the starting location at any time to refresh the duration of the Guise status. If it has already expired, it will be granted anew.
Certain duties require that you escort an NPC to a designated location while guarding them from enemy attacks. Should you stray too far from the NPC or they are attacked, they will stop moving.
The escort attempt will fail if the NPC is incapacitated, you stray too far from them, or you change areas. In the event of failure, you may return to the starting point and try again.

To grasp the fundamentals of working with familiars, first try to complete an instinctual combo with your Cu Sith.

Familiars accumulate TP via their auto-attacks, and beastmasters accumulate TP by completing weaponskill combos. Once you and your Cu Sith each have 100 TP, you are ready to perform an instinctual combo.

column2: Step Two: Complete the Instinctual Combo
column3:
Order your Cu Sith to perform its **Trick**. Then, **within seven seconds**, execute the beastmaster action **Avalanche Axe**. This will complete a **Rampant** instinctual combo!

You may complete instinctual combos with any familiar, and may trigger different actions depending on the skills used.

By working together, a beastmaster and their familiar can chain **instinctual skills**, which expend TP, to complete special combos that deal additional damage. Either a beastmaster or their familiar can be first to strike, but the combo must be completed **within seven seconds**.

column2: That Striking Dummy's Always Looking at Me...
column3: Attacking a striking dummy will pull its attention and engage you in combat. When you have finished practice, target the striking dummy and select **Reset Striking Dummy Enmity** via the subcommand menu to put it to rest.

To extend your knowledge of working with familiars, first try to complete an intentional combo with your Cu Sith.

As with instinctual combos, beastmasters and their familiars will each need to accumulate 100 TP. Complete beastmaster weaponskill combos and let your Cu Sith auto-attack until you both have 100 TP.

column2: Step Two: Complete the Intentional Combo
column3:
Order your Cu Sith to perform its **Trick**. Then, **within seven seconds**, execute the beastmaster action **Mistral Axe**. This will complete a **Moonstalker** intentional combo!

You may complete intentional combos with any familiar, and may trigger a different action depending upon the skills used.

The four basic instinctual affinities are as follows: **Volant**, **Rampant**, **Durant**, and **Eldritch**. Both beastmaster and familiar skills possess these affinities, and understanding the impact they have on one another is crucial to advanced beastmastery. Instinctual affinities can be confirmed in a weaponskill's help text, or may be intuited from the icon.

When instinctual affinities are connected in a certain order, they complete the aforementioned **intentional combos**, which in turn have two additional instinctual affinities: **Moonstalker** and **Sunstrider**.

Gaining the effect of **Moonstalker** requires chaining the following instinctual affinities:
　・**Rampant** → **Durant**
　・**Eldritch** → **Volant**
Your Cu Sith's **Trick** has a **Rampant** affinity, so when completed with **Mistral Axe**, it triggers a **Moonstalker** intentional combo.

Gaining the effect of **Sunstrider** requires chaining the following instinctual affinities:
　・**Volant** → **Rampant**
　・**Durant** → **Eldritch**
So long as instinctual affinities are performed in the designated order, it does not matter whether a beastmaster or familiar strikes first. In this case, since your Cu Sith's **Trick** has a **Rampant** affinity, preceding it with the beastmaster action **Gale Axe** will complete a **Sunstrider** intentional combo.

column2: Step One: Accumulate Stacks of Mastered Instinct
column3:
To perfect your synchronicity with your familiars, first try to complete an infinitive combo with your Cu Sith.

Spending three stacks of **Mastered Instinct** when executing **Rally** will instantly grant you 250 TP. You will need this later, so first accumulate three stacks of Mastered Instinct by completing instinctual or intentional combos with beastmaster skills. **Your Cu Sith must attack first to accumulate stacks of Mastered Instinct.**

column2: Step Two: Complete a **Moonstalker** Intentional Combo
column3:
With three stacks of Mastered Instinct on hand, it's time for an intentional combo.

Order your Cu Sith to perform its **Trick**, then execute the beastmaster action **Mistral Axe** to complete a **Moonstalker** intentional combo.

**From this point, you will have seven seconds to complete the infinitive combo.** Move with haste!

column2: Step Three: Use Rally to Accumulate 250 TP
column3: Execute **Rally** to spend all three stacks of Mastered Instinct and instantly gain 250 TP. Reaching 250 TP will change your four instinctual skills to those with affinities of **Sunstrider** or **Moonstalker**.

column2: Step Four: Complete the Infinitive Combo (Universality)
column3:
Since you gained the effect of **Moonstalker** in step two, you must execute either **Brutal Rage** or **Risen Fall**, as both weaponskills have a **Sunstrider** affinity. **An applicable action must be executed within seven seconds of completing the previous intentional combo.**

In other words, chaining the instinctual affinities **Moonstalker** and **Sunstrider** (or vice versa) will complete a **Universality** infinitive combo!

1. Accumulate three stacks of **Mastered Instinct**.
2. Complete a **Moonstalker** intentional combo.
3. Use **Rally** to gain 250 TP, thereby changing your beastmaster instinctual skills.
4. Execute an instinctual skill with a **Sunstrider** affinity.

You may complete infinitive combos with any familiar and initiate with either **Moonstalker** or **Sunstrider** affinities. In other words, illuminating your entire Inner Compass will achieve **Universality**.

Infinitive combos are considered the pinnacle of cooperation between beastmaster and familiar, as they unleash the potential of both **Sunstrider** and **Moonstalker** affinities.

The infinitive combo **Universality** is the most potent attack in a beastmaster's arsenal, so advanced practitioners are encouraged to bring this power to bear when facing challenging foes.
